content.text:
You will be given the contents of a single Discord command definition JSON (the 'command JSON'). Produce a corrected and fully localized version of that same command JSON.

This task MUST translate and/or correct ALL localized fields: both the top-level 'name_localizations' and 'description_localizations' for the command, AND for each option the 'name_localizations' and 'description_localizations' under that option.

Important rule (do not ignore): do NOT leave any localization block literally equal to the English base string across the locales. In other words, do not copy the English name or description into the localized maps for all locales. If a direct translation is not possible, produce a reasonable localized variant (transliteration, a short paraphrase, or a language-appropriate identifier) rather than returning the English text unchanged for every locale.

REQUIRED LOCALES (must appear exactly as keys): bg, cs, da, de, el, en-GB, en-US, es-419, es-ES, fi, fr, hi, hr, hu, id, it, ja, ko, lt, nl, no, pl, pt-BR, ro, ru, sv-SE, th, tr, uk, vi, zh-CN, zh-TW

Exact instructions (follow step-by-step):
1) Output EXACTLY one JSON object — the complete updated command JSON (same top-level keys). No surrounding text or explanation. Use unescaped Unicode.
2) For the top-level command: ensure 'name_localizations' contains a localized name for EVERY required locale and 'description_localizations' contains a localized description for EVERY required locale. If the input already has localized values, REVIEW them and FIX any that are incorrect, literal copies of the base English, or that violate the rules below.
3) For each option (if present): ensure option.name_localizations and option.description_localizations exist for EVERY required locale. Review and fix any existing localized entries as needed.
4) You may update the base 'name' and 'description' if necessary to meet Discord constraints; if updated, ensure consistency with localized maps.

Strict constraints (must be satisfied):
- CHAT_INPUT commands (parsed.type === 1):
  - name (base) and every localized name must match: ^[-_'\p{L}\p{N}\p{sc=Deva}\p{sc=Thai}]{1,32}$ (1–32 characters; allowed: letters, numbers, hyphen -, underscore _, apostrophe '). No spaces.
  - All caseful characters must be lowercase where applicable.
  - description (base) and each localized description must be 1–100 characters inclusive.
  - option names (base and localized) must follow the same name rule (1–32 chars). Option descriptions (base and localized) must be 1–100 chars.
- USER/MESSAGE commands (parsed.type > 1):
  - name and name_localizations must be 1–32 chars. There must be NO description or description_localizations in the final JSON for these types.

Quality and preservation rules:
- Preserve placeholders exactly (examples: {user}, {vc}, {limit}, {count}, {{placeholder}}). Do NOT translate or alter placeholders or their braces.
- Prefer natural, concise translations appropriate for a command name in each language. If a natural translation contains spaces or invalid chars, transform spaces to single hyphens '-', remove other disallowed characters, lowercase caseful letters, and truncate to <=32 characters. Do this only when necessary; prefer a natural short translation over mechanical slugging when possible.
- If an input locale value is already present but incorrect or literal-English, correct it — do NOT leave it as the English source.
- If no reasonable translation exists, produce a localized variant (e.g., transliteration or concise paraphrase) instead of leaving the English text unchanged for every locale.
- Truncate descriptions at sensible word boundaries (<=100 chars) and avoid splitting placeholders.
- Preserve all other JSON fields (id, type, default_permission, options array structure). Only add/replace localized name/description maps and translated strings.
Now: output the fully updated command JSON object and nothing else.
